name: Chasmanthium

project_scope.selection_mode: FINISH/ENRICH one already canonical species; not full county flora
project_scope.native_zone_status: Existing fields unchanged; separate native-by-county audit paused.

look_here_first: ONE CURRENTLY INSTALLED GENUS SPECIES, Chasmanthium latifolium. Follow a long drooping 10–30 mm slender pedicel to ONE fish-like laterally FLATTENED 20–40 mm spikelet on an open nodding panicle. That large spikelet holds many pointed overlapping FLORETS, each of which is not an individual loose seed. Other Chasmanthium (C. laxum/C. sessiliflorum) usually have far smaller spikelets on short stalks and more ascending or contracted panicles. When sterile, check broad jointed leafy culm and ~0.7-mm membranous/ciliate true ligule with 10–20×; not shown in available photos.

recognition.where_to_look_first: First follow the arching seedhead axis to its thin pendant spikelet stalk. Then zoom into one large, flattened shingled spikelet. Finally view alternate wide leaves along a jointed stem and inspect the tiny ciliate-membranous ligule at the true blade/sheath junction.
priority: wide grass blades roughly 8–20 mm broad, alternating along stems
loose curving/drooping terminal panicle, roughly 15–30 cm in local guide
very flattened multi-flowered spikelet about 20–40 mm long, often hanging like a fish
long slender spikelet pedicel typically 10–30 mm rather than short stalk
overlapping zigzag/chevron rows of lemmas on spikelet face
short rhizomatous perennial spreading in moist shaded woodland undergrowth
short finely ciliate-membranous true ligule; requires close photo

comparison_lesson.memory_rule: LARGE 20–40 mm FLAT many-flowered fish + 10–30 mm LONG DANGLING stalk = inland sea oats candidate; other woodoats shorter stalks and much smaller spikelets; actual flowers are overlapping bracts NOT loose grain.
quick_split: C. latifolium — large, broad, pendant spikelets on long threadlike stalks; curved open flowering head, broad leaves.
C. laxum — smaller spikelets borne closely against narrower, more ascending/contracted panicle branches; no large hanging 'fish'.
C. sessiliflorum — smaller almost unstalked spikelets along rather erect branches, often hairy leaf sheaths; not same big dangling units.
Uniola paniculata — dune/coast sea oats, different genus and ecology, not a local woodland sea oats concept.
Briza spp. — smaller drooping quaking spikelets; inspect head architecture and floral anatomy before assigning identity.
comparison_lesson.lookalike_caution: Photo panel 4 is an authored public-domain Jim Conrad close-up from Mississippi, not Texas provenance. It demonstrates overlapping florets only; per-photo true glumes, caryopsis and measured ligule not proved. Native range of C. laxum/C. sessiliflorum comparison concepts remains unreviewed.

comparisons.name: Slender / spike woodoats
comparisons.distinction: Inland sea oats has very large flat spikelets roughly 20–40 mm long, dangling on long slender pedicels (often 10–30 mm) from nodding branches. C. laxum has much smaller spikelets (often ~5–8 mm) on very short stalks, generally in slender, upright or ascending contracted branches. Vegetative foliage is usually narrower, but use a flowering plant to confirm.
comparisons.caution: Old floras may include the sessiliflorum concept under laxum at varietal rank. Do not silently merge or create another accepted taxon.

comparisons.name: Longleaf woodoats
comparisons.distinction: More narrow/contracted upright-to-ascending panicle, short spikelet stalks, small spikelets, and commonly hairy leaf sheaths/collars. C. latifolium has larger conspicuously flat dangling spikelets on long slender stalks and smoother sheaths.
comparisons.caution: Name/rank treatments vary regionally; local county occurrence needs separate BONAP/NAPA review.

comparisons.name: Coastal sea oats
comparisons.distinction: Can also show broad flattened spikelets but typically grows as a robust sand-dune grass with different floral characters and inflorescence proportions. It is not the shady woodland/streambank inland sea oats. Habitat alone does not prove identity.
comparisons.caution: Do not treat the common name 'sea oats' as proof two genera are interchangeable or as a Hays County-native record.

comparisons.name: Quaking grasses
comparisons.distinction: Both have nodding flat spikelets but generally different leaf proportions, flowerhead architecture and dangling units. Verify node/stalk arrangement, each spikelet's florets and actual local presence. Briza spp. are introduced in much of the U.S.
comparisons.caution: Not a claim these are common native Hays grasses.

comparisons.name: Confusion with broadleaf sedges / bamboo-like grass
comparisons.distinction: Without seedheads, locate a rounded jointed grass culm, alternating sheathing grass leaves, minute ciliate-membranous ligule and short rhizomatous growth. Broad grass leaves alone cannot guarantee species.
comparisons.caution: Require blooming specimens or keep to Chasmanthium sp. when inconclusive.

what_to_teach_crew: First follow ONE hanging spikelet on its actual long slender stalk, not a vague leaf silhouette or woodland habitat.
One fish-shaped object is ONE compressed MULTI-FLORETED spikelet; its overlapping pointed florets are not one seed each.
Use source-licensed photographs for panicle, dried winter leaves and whole spikelet; macro panel 4 from Jim Conrad is public-domain nonlocal learning reference.
Compare C. laxum and C. sessiliflorum short-stalked small ascending spikelets, not a new county nativity determination.
At next field visit photograph a true ligule/sheath with mm scale, intact attachment of spikelet, glumes and ripe caryopsis; nothing in these photos proves those details.

visual_comparison.title: Chasmanthium — actual many-flowered dangling fish spikelet, genuine grain and rhizome
visual_comparison.subtitle: Public-educational genus card now links seven Bob Harms source-identified Central Texas closeups to the four existing original broad views. Teaching: long individual stalk → flattened spikelet → repeated fertile lemmas → grain between lemma/palea; rhizome; true sheath and collar; exact thin ligule tip still a gap.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: FISH ON A LINE ≠ ONE SEED: EACH 20–40mm fish-shape is a SPIKELET with many distinct FLORETS and pointed LEMMAS. One dark actual CARYOPSIS is held inside its LEMMA+PALEA. Broad leaf, underground scaly RHIZOME; tiny membranous ligule where blade meets sheath. Compare much smaller and less-stalked laxum/sessiliflorum, don't infer native-by-county from photos.

items.label: 1 · Flat overlapping oat-like spikelets — flowering head
items.image_role: Close view of many broad flattened spikelets dangling on slender stalks from a curved inflorescence axis
items.caption: Actually inspected canonical Susan Elliott photo: curved flowering panicle with many separate, flattened, oat-like hanging MULTI-FLORETED spikelets, each on a visible thin drooping pedicel. The pointed shinglelike bracts form a repeated pattern. These structures, not individual loose seeds or glume measurements, are what the arrows mark.
items.why_it_matters: This single image teaches the excellent field distinction: pendant 'fish-shaped' spikelets on long thin stalks, instead of a narrow ascending seedhead.
items.creator: Susan Elliott
items.photo_status: Original CC BY-NC Susan Elliott 1024×768 archived JPEG re-inspected 2026-10-21; four markers on clearly visible curved axis, long stalk, flattened spikelet and stacked floret bracts; local taxon identification inherited from original source, not separately vouchered.

items.label: 2 · Dry-season plant and hanging spikelets
items.image_role: Actual archived species-tagged dry-season patch: broad dry blades and pendant spikelets amid woodland litter
items.caption: Original Nathan May CC BY photo examined: dormant straw-coloured clump with broad curling dried blades and many pale dangling spikelets. Multiple plants and stems intermingle; no attached rhizome or individual leaf ligule can be proven from this frame.
items.why_it_matters: Crew can recognize inland sea oats when tan and dormant, not just in green summer conditions.
items.creator: Nathan May
items.photo_status: Canonically archived Nathan May CC BY JPEG inspected again 2026-10-21; two visible coarse habit arrows; per-photo exact CC license version retains archival uncertainty.

items.label: 3 · Broad blade beside hand, mature dry panicle
items.image_role: Dried broad grass leaf blades in hand and thin dangling panicle segments in front, giving field size context
items.caption: Original CC0 source-determined photo held in hand: broad dry grass blade crosses the fingers, alongside thinner flowering axes and several hanging papery spikelets. The photo does NOT show a measured ligule, exposed rhizome or individual caryopsis. Do not treat a loose dry bract as an identifiable grain.
items.why_it_matters: Shows the broad grass foliage and hanging dried spikelets together, especially useful without green leaves.
items.creator: sonoresmore
items.photo_status: Canonical sonoressmore CC0 original inspected 2026-10-21; visible broad blade and hanging spikelets only, fine anatomy unclaimed.

items.label: 4 · CLOSE — one flattened spikelet with overlapping florets (Mississippi example)
items.image_role: Single macro of source-identified Chasmanthium latifolium flattened spikelet showing overlapping pointed green lemma/bract structures, photographed by Jim Conrad in Mississippi
items.caption: Jim Conrad's original 400×678 public-domain photo shows numerous overlapping pointed floret bracts along ONE strongly flattened spikelet. It is not a photograph of 10 individual grains: florets contain the future grains. The file's description identifies two glumes at the upper end, but individual basal parts cannot be independently distinguished with precision here, so arrows label only the visible overlapping units and whole spikelet.
items.why_it_matters: Teaches why each pendant fish-shaped unit is ONE multi-flowered spikelet, instead of a single seed, and connects whole seedhead recognition to true component architecture.
items.creator: Jim Conrad
items.origin_context: Mississippi example; not a Hays County voucher or locality evidence
items.photo_status: PUBLIC DOMAIN Jim Conrad exact source 400×678 JPEG physically saved and original SHA1 verified 2026-10-21; altered only by EXIF-free JPEG re-encode, source/photo credit retained. Photo points to overlapping florets/flat spikelet, no individual glume/caryopsis dissection. Original Mississippi photo, no Hays provenance.

items.label: NEW · Green panicle — every flat fish is ONE full spikelet · PROVISIONAL PHOTO REVIEW
items.image_role: Actual flowering branch/panicle with many broad strongly compressed green spikelets, each on its own visibly thin descending pedicel; original left-side photographed physical scale.
items.caption: Real source-labelled Chasmanthium latifolium green panicle. Follow a slender branching stalk to each hanging flat fish-shaped SPIKELET; one such 'fish' contains multiple FLORETS. The pale white lines are exposed midribs and edges of overlapping LEMMAS, not individual veins on a single seed. Source includes an actual size scale, but precise one-pedicel length not independently measured.

items.label: NEW · REAL FLORET DISSECTION — lemmas, paleas and enclosed dark caryopsis · PROVISIONAL PHOTO REVIEW
items.image_role: Actual Bob Harms mature floral parts of Chasmanthium latifolium photographed separated broad-side/edgewise under source metric scale. Far-right partially opened lemma/palea encloses a real dark brown caryopsis (true grain). Subtle individual glumes from separate outer spikelet not independently shown.
items.caption: This genuine anatomy plate finally shows separate floral BRACTS and a DARK BROWN TRUE GRAIN. At FAR RIGHT the enclosing scales are opened around the caryopsis; other detached long pointed pieces show surface/edge views of the floret's lemma/palea. Glumes are the two small OUTER bracts at the base of a full spikelet — do not invent a 'glume' arrow on these individually detached florets. The source has a real top scale, but single-bract measurements are not independently verified.

items.image_role: Source-verified actual inland sea oats shallow scaly horizontal rhizome segments linking several upright culm bases, roots, overlapping dried sheaths and buds, with original scale at left. Exact source location/date not independently established.

The <=1 mm true jagged-membranous ligule margin is not separately clear enough to label, contrast between hooded blade/sheath and inner translucent margin is subtle.
items.caption: Correct botanical location: the leaf blade departs from its clasping/opened SHEATH at this junction. The broad brown flap is mostly older sheath tissue; never label the whole flap 'ligule'.
